notes.title: Announcing the spooky successor to Cosmic Express! 🎃
notes.notes:
Hey there!

We have some very exciting news for fans of [b]Cosmic Express[/b]. If you enjoyed planning the train route for the world's most awkward space colony... Then things are about to get a lot spookier 🎃

Announcing: [b][url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3352310/Spooky_Express/]Spooky Express[/url][/b]!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/7938465/83e82ab61856c744ba366a8e814e5b0fc8468bd8.png[/img]

Plan the train route for the world’s spookiest theme park!
All the passengers are all just [i]dying[/i] to ride the Spooky Express.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/7938465/ae096275ed36a1d1ae8b7fd51d4e66ba6d0c68c1.gif[/img]

Pick up the creepy cryptids and drop them at their destinations around the park. But be careful! Don’t let them scare or bite the human passengers. Stay [i]on track[/i] of the situation or you’ll have a [i]grave[/i] problem.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/3352310/Spooky_Express/

Spooky Express is great follow-up to the award-winning thinky puzzle game, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/583270/Cosmic_Express/]Cosmic Express[/url] and will feature over 100 brand new and unique levels with countless monsters, maps and mechanics.

If that sounds like something you might be interested in, please give us a wishlist on Steam, or share the trailer below.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uewJWzD6s10

...And that's not all. If you want to hear even more about Spooky Express, we've just released a special episode of the [url=https://www.draknek.org/podcast]Draknek & Friends Official Podcast[/url]. Tune in wherever you get your podcasts to hear creative director Alan Hazelden and producer Syrenne McNulty chat to the level designer Lucas Le Slo about the development of the game, and some of the other projects he's involved in.

Until next time 👋

notes.title: Cosmic Express collides with Sokobond in new game puzzle Sokobond Express
notes.notes:
What happens when you combine two great puzzle games? You get one puzzle game which makes me, an accredited professional fool, feel dizzy with noncomprehension. That game is Sokobond Express, which launched yesterday and combines the atom-shoving chemistry of Sokobond with the route-planning puzzling of Cosmic Express. So you have to draw paths around a grid to gather atoms to correctly build a desired molecule. That's all. Just molecular chemistry and pathing, at the same time. Oh, my poor foolish head.

Read more

notes.title: Sokobond Express is available today!
notes.notes:
We are thrilled to share that Sokobond Express, a beautifully minimalist puzzle game that combines chemical bonds and puzzling pathfinding in novel ways, is out on Steam now. Please enjoy and leave a Steam review!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1701330/Sokobond_Express/

Sokobond Express is developed by José Hernández, a first time commercial developer living in Venezuela. After several years of hard work and refining the game until it felt just right, Hernández is excited for players to finally be able to play it.

“Working on Sokobond Express for the last three years has been a real joy. I think the hardest thing to pull off in the game was the pacing - making levels get progressively harder while remaining engaging took a really long time. We spent a lot of time redesigning early-game levels to make them the perfect difficulty. We're really proud of how things ended up, so please check it out!”- José Hernández

If you’re a fan of other Draknek games, we know Sokobond Express  will be right up your alley. 
It combines the pathfinding of Cosmic Express with the deep but elegant atom building from Sokobond - paying homage to its predecessors while also being an elegant and entrancing game of its own.

Finally, the game is Steam Deck verified. Whether you're playing on Windows, macOS, Linux, or the Steam Deck, the game should provide a native and excellent play experience.

We can’t wait for you to play this puzzle masterpiece.

Thanks,
Draknek & Friends

This game lines up perfectly with our portfolio of games like A Monster’s Expedition, and if you’ve liked our past games, we’re confident you’ll love this one too.

[previewyoutube=nlRYgY-Oa30;full][/previewyoutube]

If you’re excited for the game like us and want to get a notification as soon as the game releases, be sure to wishlist the game:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1147890/Bonfire_Peaks/

Move onwards, move upwards, and leave nothing behind: in Bonfire Peaks, players must climb to the top of a mysterious island ruin, burning everything they own along the way. Featuring hours of masterfully designed puzzle content, a breathtakingly lovely voxel overworld, and not a single second of filler content.

2021 is shaping up to be Draknek & Friends’ biggest year ever, and we can’t wait to share all that we have in store for you.

notes.title: A Monster's Expedition - out now!
notes.notes:
[i]A Monster's Expedition (Through Puzzling Exhibitions)[/i], the new game from Draknek & Friends, is now available on Steam!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1052990/A_Monsters_Expedition/

[img]https://cdn.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/33018631/8dd944316309f122ece24e8fdcf66f2095d5c666.png[/img]

I know everyone says this, but I think we've made something really something special that almost everyone will enjoy. The puzzles lead to dozens upon dozens of "a-ha" moments, and vary in difficulty throughout the open world. Anyone should be able to get to the end, but those who are looking for a more difficult experience will be more than satisfied by hundreds of challenging optional puzzles and secrets.

[list]
[*]From the team that brought you the award winning puzzle games Sokobond, A Good Snowman is Hard to Build, and Cosmic Express

notes.title: A Monster's Expedition is a tree-pushing puzzler from the creators of Cosmic Express
notes.notes:
I often wish I had the mind for puzzle games. Alan “Draknek” Hazelden’s catalogue of deceptively hard brainteasers look bleedin’ lovely, but I simply can’t be screaming at my monitor with strangers in the office. After solving lunar train dilemmas with Cosmic Express and teaching us that A Good Snowman Is Hard To Build, Draknek And Friends are returning with A Monster’s Expedition – pushing over trees to explore a water-logged museum of human ruin on Steam and Itch.io later this year.

notes.title: Charting the puzzle depths of Cosmic Express
notes.notes:
This is The Mechanic, where Alex Wiltshire invites developers to discuss the inner workings of their games. This time, Cosmic Express [official site].

There are many reasons why puzzle games designed by Alan Draknek Hazelden sit on top of the form. There s the puzzles, for one thing. They re pretty good. They explore seemingly simple rulesets and find in them huge and satisfying challenge, dragging you along for the ride. That s as true for Cosmic Express as for all Hazelden s games. (Actually, maybe that s sort of literally true, since Cosmic Express is about drawing tracks to take aliens on little train rides.)

But there s something else to his puzzles, something that opens up a sense of wonder at the depth of the little logical worlds that emerge from their rulesets and layouts. It s also something that gives you a sense of involvement and discovery in a genre that can so often feel like jumping through a designer s tortuous hoops. It s that they have:

notes.title: Assessing frustration in Cosmic Express playtests
notes.notes:
While out at GDC I spent a bit of time chatting to Alan Hazelden about Cosmic Express [official site], his train-themed logic puzzler. I was playing the preview build of the game at the time and was curious to know a bit more about how you go about sorting the levels for a difficulty curve and how you interpret good and bad kinds of frustration when playtesting a puzzle game.

It was an interesting chat, punctuated by the arrival of a little dog partway through, so I’m going to just pull out a few of the observations which inform the difficulty curve discussion. It’s nice to have it as an accompaniment to yesterday’s the review. … [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Wot I Think: Cosmic Express
notes.notes:
Here it is! The space game review you’ve all been waiting for on this, Monday the twentieth of March, 2017: Cosmic Express!

Cosmic Express [official site] is an adorable-but-also-rock-solid puzzle game from Alan Hazelden. He’s working with Ben Davis who was his collaborator on RPS favourite, A Good Snowman…, and with Tyu of the Klondike collective. The result is a really satisfying puzzle game where you lay the track for a train in order to transport little alien blobs to their destinations. … [visit site to read more]

notes.title: Spacetrain puzzler Cosmic Express chug chuggas out
notes.notes: The intergalactic planetary puzzling of Cosmic Express [official site] has pulled into the station. It looks lovely and sounds simple but I’d expect fiendish puzzling as it’s made by folks from such fine head-scratchers as A Good Snowman Is Hard To Build and Sokobond.
